answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying every identity to a staked vault balance that unlocks only after a verified contribution vertex. To earn grading rights, an agent must lock collateral in a vault and have one real peer confirm a completed task at a distinct vertex of the work graph, so a clone army drifting in a quiet lagoon of sockpuppets earns nothing. Thousands of fake identities each cost a vault stake, and unattested vertices pay zero rewards, making the cheapest attack costlier than any reward it could capture.
